Solvency II standard formula: non-life premium and reserve risk

Source: R/solvency.R
sii_premium_reserve_risk.Rd

The capital requirement for non-life premium and reserve risk of the Solvency II standard formula (Articles 115 to 117 of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35), from the volume measures of each segment.

Usage

sii_premium_reserve_risk(
  volumes,
  np_adjustment = NULL,
  premium_sd = NULL,
  reserve_sd = NULL
)

Arguments

volumes

A data frame with a row per segment the undertaking writes: its segment (the number, 1 to 12, of sii_nonlife_segments), its premium and reserve volume measures, and optionally its geographical diversification (1 when not given).

np_adjustment

The segments whose premium standard deviation takes the 80% adjustment for non-proportional reinsurance: NULL (the default) for none, or some of 1, 4 and 5.

premium_sd, reserve_sd

Undertaking-specific standard deviations replacing the standard ones, named by segment number (such as c("4" = 0.06)), or NULL.

Value

A list with by_segment, a data frame with each segment's volumes, its standard deviations, its volume measure and its capital on its own (\(3 \sigma_s V_s\)); total, the volume measure, the standard deviation, the capital requirement, the sum of the segments' capital and the diversification between them; and reserve_risk and premium_risk, the capital of each risk alone (the same formula with the other volume set to zero).

Details

The standard deviation of a segment combines those of its premium and reserve risk with a correlation of 50%: $$\sigma_s = \frac{\sqrt{(\sigma_{p,s} V_{p,s})^2 + \sigma_{p,s} \sigma_{r,s} V_{p,s} V_{r,s} + (\sigma_{r,s} V_{r,s})^2}}{V_{p,s} + V_{r,s}},$$ and its volume is \(V_s = (V_{p,s} + V_{r,s}) (0.75 + 0.25 DIV_s)\), with \(DIV_s\) its geographical diversification (1 for business in a single region). The segments are joined with the correlations \(CorrS\) of Annex IV: \(\sigma = \sqrt{\sum_{s,t} CorrS_{s,t} \sigma_s V_s \sigma_t V_t} / V\), with \(V = \sum_s V_s\), and the capital requirement is \(3 \sigma V\).

The premium volume of a segment is, under Article 116, the larger of the earned premium of the next year and of the last year, plus the expected premiums of existing and future contracts beyond the next year; the reserve volume is its best estimate of the claims provision, net of reinsurance. They are given here; the function does not derive them. The adjustment for non-proportional reinsurance (80% of the premium standard deviation of segments 1, 4 and 5, Article 117(3)) is applied to the segments asked for, where the undertaking's reinsurance qualifies.

References

Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35, Articles 115 to 117 and Annexes II and IV, as amended by Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/981.

See also

sii_nonlife_segments, risk_adjustment.

Examples

volumes <- data.frame(segment = c(1, 2, 4), premium = c(40e6, 25e6, 30e6),
                      reserve = c(60e6, 10e6, 20e6))
sii <- sii_premium_reserve_risk(volumes)
sii$total
#>          volume              sd         capital      standalone diversification 
#>    1.850000e+08    6.123274e-02    3.398417e+07    4.345331e+07    9.469133e+06 
sii$by_segment[, c("name", "sd", "volume", "capital")]
#>                                name         sd  volume  capital
#> 1           Motor vehicle liability 0.08170679 1.0e+08 24512038
#> 2                       Other motor 0.07137141 3.5e+07  7493998
#> 3 Fire and other damage to property 0.07631514 5.0e+07 11447270
